glosses: A mixture of two or more things.

glosses: A word formed by combining two other words; a grammatical contamination, portmanteau word.

examples.text: Blends, also known as portmanteau words, are not an original part of English. That is, none occur in Old or Middle English, nor even in Elizabethan English, with the earliest known example being the rare and now obsolete term tomaxe, a blend of tomahawk and axe.

glosses: To mingle; to mix; to unite intimately; to pass or shade insensibly into each other.

examples.text: To make hummus you need to blend chickpeas, olive oil, lemon juice and garlic.

glosses: To be mingled or mixed.

Earless ghost swift moths become “invisible” to echolocating bats by forming mating clusters close[…]above vegetation and effectively blending into the clutter of echoes that the bat receives from the leaves and stems around them. Many insects probably use this strategy, which is a close analogy to crypsis in the visible world—camouflage and other methods for blending into one’s visual background.
